action: Calc I: tangent line with the product rule
details: Find the equation of the tangent line to f(x) = x^2 * sin(x) at x = pi.
solution:
Product rule: f'(x) = 2x*sin(x) + x^2*cos(x).
At x = pi: sin(pi) = 0 and cos(pi) = -1, so f'(pi) = 0 + pi^2*(-1) = -pi^2.
Point: f(pi) = pi^2 * 0 = 0, so the point is (pi, 0).
Tangent line: y = -pi^2 (x - pi), i.e. y = -pi^2 x + pi^3.
resource_title: Paul's Notes: Product and Quotient Rule

action: Full Council: YES, the Grok Build link is safe to run unattended (after 5 fixes)
question: Is the Agent City <-> Grok Build interchange (public feed, manifest updater, city_apply helper, council gate) safe, cheap, and reliable enough to run unattended on the owner's machine every session?
reason: Integrity, process-once, rollback and resource limits are tested (68 tests, ubuntu + macOS CI) and every change still needs a local council YES plus passing checks and tests. Dissent (Devil's Advocate): `grok inspect` output and hook-before-rules ordering are unverified on a real Grok Build install, so global items may fail and roll back until confirmed.
details: Lean Full Council (14 seats, King, Red Team), red-teaming both ends. Fixed this session: (1) Risk Officer: allowlisted commands could still write files (sort -o, uniq OUT, eslint/ruff --fix, tsc without --noEmit, git --output, git grep -O pager); now refused at both ends. (2) Systems Thinker: city roles could flood the queue and the owner's token budget; build fails over 3 gb items a day. (3) First-Principles: updater worst case (9 downloads) exceeded the 20 s hook timeout; now a 12 s budget, the rest waits. (4) Red Team: a session killed mid-apply leaves a half-applied change with an expired claim; `next` now reports unfinished journals and the skill rolls back only after checking the diff. (5) Red Team: editing a published change text re-queues it under a new id; AGENTS.md now forbids it. Also found by the tests: test runs leave __pycache__ files, which failed every after-check; new untracked files are now reported but never committed, and undeclared tracked edits still fail. Accepted risks: a compromised public repo can change rules and skills (checksums prove integrity, not origin; mitigated by the allowlist, council gate, updates.log, off and pin switches); feed commands can read files the owner can read (output stays local); python3 is required.
ideals: Fits 1, 4, 6 and 7 (real work, token-light, private, autonomous). Tension with 3 (seamless): python3 is required and global items stay unverified until a real session; accepted because failures roll back and are reported, never silent.
